newsitem.title: INDIA: Almost 300 killed in Indian cyclone.
newsitem.headline: Almost 300 killed in Indian cyclone.

text.p: The death toll from a cyclone that struck India's major crop-growing state of Andhra Pradesh has climbed to nearly 300, state-run Doordarshan television said on Thursday.
"This is the worst cyclone in 10 years," H.S. Brahma, the chief state official coordinating relief operations, told Reuters.

The storm, with winds of between 100 and 120 kmph (60 and 75 mph), struck India's southeast coast on Wednesday evening, flattening homes, destroying crops and cutting transport and communication links. But it appeared to weakening on Thursday.
Authorities in Hyderabad, the capital of Andhra Pradesh, said most of the deaths were due to flooding, houses collapsing and electrocutions.
"Nearly 300 were killed and crops were damaged extensively in the Andhra Pradesh cyclonic storm," Doordarshan said.
State government officials earlier put the number of deaths at 234 but said they expected the figure to climb.
"The toll may be very high, and it may even touch 1,000," the state's Chief Minister V. Chandrababu Naidu told reporters soon after he surveyed the flooded areas by helicopter.
The cyclone crossed the coast 50 km (30 miles) south of the port of Kakinada. Communications were disrupted after it wreaked havoc in the rich rice-growing Godavari river delta, officials said.
In East Godavari, where 100,000 homes were destroyed or damaged, at least 169 people have died. Authorities said 42 of them were killed when a boat capsized in the Godavari river.
Nearly 200,000 people were evacuated from their homes and moved to higher ground after water levels rose two metres (six feet) high in some villages, officials said.

The floods washed away the standing rice crop over an area of 8.5 million hectares (22 million acres), Doordarshan said. An additional 1.9 million hectares (4.8 million acres) of cultivable land was also swamped, it said.
"There has been large scale damage of plantation crops -- mostly coconut and bananas, and other horticultural produce," Brahma said.
The cyclone appeared to be petering out on Thursday.

"The system (depression) is weakening," C.V.V. Bhadram, director of the Meteorological Centre, said. He aded that the cyclone had moved deeper inland and was was likely to head in a west-north-west direction.

Local government officials have been alerted to deal with the impact of the storm. Businesses, offices, and schools have been shut till Sunday. The government has asked the military to help with relief operations.
The district administration is providing grains and drinking water to all those who lost their homes.
Last month, floods damaged 1.13 million hectares (3.1 million acres) of land, about eight per cent of farmed areas in Andhra Pradesh.
